content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day window, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates prices in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, then gradually converges toward true values — suggesting lagged response to recent trends.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 76+), model overreacts with exaggerated subsequent peaks, then undercorrects.
- Mean reversion is not fully captured: model holds onto high forecasts longer than true values show.
- Model tends to underestimate low-price periods (e.g., 65–68 range) and overestimates them when they occur after a dip.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward lower values in the second half of the 30-day window, especially when true values are rising.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or cyclical patterns — e.g., consistently underpredicts price rebounds after low points.
- Horizon-specific: 10–15 day forecasts are most prone to underestimation; 20+ day forecasts show more lag and overshoot.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — once a price falls, it doesn’t quickly recover, even if true values show rebound.
